summary: Set up automated sync of /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 (source of truth) to node2, verified it propagates changes within 15 minutes via cron (actual interval 5 min), then completed the mandatory sequential restart-and-recovery protocol on both nodes.
actions_performed: Created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 (root:root, 0644) since it did not previously exist on either node
Distributed the cluster SSH keypair: pubkey added to node1's antrieb authorized_keys, privkey installed on node2
Wrote /usr/local/bin/sync-inventory-app-conf.sh on node2: SSHes to node1, fetches app.conf via sudo cat, and installs it locally only if content changed (checksum compare, idempotent)
Installed a */5 min crontab entry on node2 running the sync script via sudo -n (well under the 15-minute requirement)

Diagnosed and fixed two bugs: RHEL7 OpenSSH 7.4 doesn't support StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new (switched to no + /dev/null known_hosts), and the original crontab entry ran unprivileged and silently failed to write the root-owned destination file (fixed by invoking via sudo -n)
Hardened node1 resolution with a static /etc/hosts entry instead of a /tmp file that might not survive reboots
Verified end-to-end: changed sync_version on node1 three times and confirmed the real unmodified cron schedule picked up each change automatically, including once after both nodes were rebooted

Captured pre-restart baselines, rebooted node1 then node2 sequentially using shutdown -r now backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until each came back, and proved boot_id changed on both
Verified post-restart recovery: sshd/crond active, crontab intact, SSH key intact, app.conf content and checksum intact on both nodes after reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 source-of-truth file created and content verified
Initial sync mechanism seeded node2 correctly
evidence.summary: Diagnosed SSH option incompatibility, fixed script, ran sync manually; node2 checksum matched node1's 1e2506bb...

evidence.requirement: Cron installed and running as correct privilege
evidence.summary: Found crontab ran unprivileged and failed silently; fixed to invoke via sudo -n and confirmed a clean-env run succeeds and writes SYNCED to log

evidence.requirement: Change on node1 propagates to node2 within 15 minutes (first real-cron proof)
evidence.summary: Changed sync_version=2->3 on node1 at 18:12:57; unmodified */5 cron fired naturally at 18:15:02 and synced; final checksums on both nodes match (e91c579e...)

evidence.requirement: Sync survives reboot and still functions afterward (second real-cron proof)
evidence.summary: After both reboots, hardened script (hostname-based node1 resolution) still works; changed sync_version=3->4 on node1, real cron fired at 18:20:01 and synced to f9f5e20a..., matching node1
